todos.description: Improve keyboard navigation in the Tags dialog
todos.context: In the Tags dialog (internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go) the button row is rebuilt by setGenerating(bool): while a run is in flight it shows Cancel (N) | Background (B) | disabled Generate, idle it shows Close (ESC) | Copy title | Copy keywords | [Save JPEG] | Generate; N and B are not handled by the dialog but by global GLFW scancode shortcuts on the canvas (internal/gui/ui/shortcuts.go, mapped to OnCancel/OnBlue and dispatched through internal/gui/app/actions.go + tags_action.go, gated by shortcutsBlocked), so they only fire when nothing holds focus and Generating() calls window.Canvas().Unfocus() as a workaround. Escape is already solved separately by the escapeEntry/escapeDateEntry/escapeCheck wrappers in internal/gui/ui/escapable.go, which intercept Escape in TypedKey and forward it to TagsDialogCallbacks.OnEscape because a Fyne calendar popup can stack over the dialog; the dialog otherwise relies on default Fyne Tab traversal across Concept, Location, Editorial, Date, claude path, Title, Keywords and the buttons, and this fragile letter-key/focus interaction is what prompted the task.

plan.summary: Move the Tags dialog's keyboard handling into the dialog itself so it no longer depends on canvas-level GLFW scancode shortcuts firing only while nothing holds focus (and on the `window.Canvas().Unfocus()` workaround in `Generating()`). The escape wrappers in internal/gui/ui/escapable.go become a general key router that every focusable widget of the dialog (entries, date entry, check, and a new button wrapper) consults before the embedded widget sees the key; multi-line entries stop swallowing Tab, so Tab traversal actually walks the whole dialog; buttons answer Return as well as Space and, while a run is going, N/B by physical key; and focus is placed deliberately (Concept on open, Cancel while a run goes, a sensible field when the run ends) instead of being cleared. Help text and CLAUDE.md are updated last. The app-side plumbing (actions.go, tags_action.go, shortcuts.go) keeps working unchanged as a fallback for when nothing in the dialog holds focus.

steps.title: Turn the escape wrappers into a key router and let Tab leave the multi-line fields
steps.details: In internal/gui/ui/escapable.go replace the `onEscape func()` field of `escapeEntry`, `escapeDateEntry` and `escapeCheck` with `onKey func(*fyne.KeyEvent) bool`: `TypedKey` calls it first and returns when it reports the key as consumed, otherwise it forwards to the embedded widget. Rename the three types to `dialogEntry`, `dialogDateEntry`, `dialogCheck` (file name stays escapable.go) and rewrite the file header comment: it is no longer only about Escape. Add `func (e *dialogEntry) AcceptsTab() bool { return false }` — the GLFW driver checks `fyne.Tabbable.AcceptsTab()` in `capturesTab` *before* `TypedKey`, so a multi-line `widget.Entry` (Title, Keywords) currently eats Tab and cannot be left by keyboard; overriding it is the only way to make Tab traverse. In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go add `func (d *TagsDialog) handleKey(ev *fyne.KeyEvent) bool` that consumes `fyne.KeyEscape` by calling `d.requestEscape()` and returns false otherwise, and pass `d.handleKey` to every constructor in `buildInputs`/`buildResult`; update the struct field types. In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog_test.go update the `[]*escapeEntry` loop in TestTagsDialog_Escape to `[]*dialogEntry` and add cases: Tab is not accepted by title/keywords (`assert.False(t, d.keywords.AcceptsTab())`) and a non-Escape key still reaches the widget (the existing "other keys still reach the input" case covers the latter).

steps.title: Give the dialog buttons keyboard activation and the run's command keys
steps.details: Add a `dialogButton` wrapper to internal/gui/ui/escapable.go embedding `widget.Button` with an `onKey func(*fyne.KeyEvent) bool`: `TypedKey` asks the dialog first, then treats `fyne.KeyReturn`/`fyne.KeyEnter` as a tap (Fyne's Button only answers Space), then falls through to `widget.Button.TypedKey`. Add a helper to internal/gui/ui/shortcuts.go, e.g. `func physicalKey(ev *fyne.KeyEvent, key glfw.Key, name fyne.KeyName) bool`, matching `ev.Physical.ScanCode == glfw.GetKeyScancode(key)` or `ev.Name == name` — the scancode form keeps the letters layout-independent like the canvas shortcuts, the name form is the fallback where GLFW is not initialised (it returns -1 then, which would make N and B collide). In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go build every button (`generateBtn`, `copyTitleBtn`, `copyKeywordsBtn`, `saveJPEGBtn`, `closeBtn`, `cancelRunBtn`, `backgroundBtn`) as `*dialogButton`, change `setEnabled(button *widget.Button, ...)` to take `*dialogButton`, and add `func (d *TagsDialog) handleCommandKey(ev *fyne.KeyEvent) bool` = `handleKey` plus, while `d.generating`, N -> `call(d.callbacks.OnCancelRun)` and B -> `call(d.callbacks.OnBackground)`; hand `handleCommandKey` to the buttons and to `dialogCheck` (neither consumes runes, so intercepting bare letters there is safe, unlike in a text entry where the character still arrives through TypedRune). Tests in internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog_test.go: N and B on the focused `cancelRunBtn` reach OnCancelRun/OnBackground only while generating; Return on a focused button taps it; N typed into `d.concept` triggers no callback.

steps.title: Place focus deliberately instead of clearing it
steps.details: In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go add a `shown bool` field set in `Show()` (cleared in `Hide()`) and a small `func (d *TagsDialog) focus(obj fyne.Focusable)` that no-ops unless the dialog is shown — `canvas.Focus` logs "Failed to focus object which is not part of the canvas' content, menu or overlays" for an object in an unshown dialog. `Show()` focuses `d.concept` so the dialog opens ready for typing. `Generating()` drops `d.window.Canvas().Unfocus()` and instead focuses `d.cancelRunBtn` after `setGenerating(true)`, so N/B/Space/Return all act on the run without the unfocus trick; update the comment above it, which explains the workaround. `finishRun()` must move focus off the button that is about to leave the row (the focus manager keeps a pointer to a removed object and keys then go nowhere): focus `d.pathEntry` when `Fail` revealed `pathRow`, `d.title` when tags arrived, else `d.generateBtn`; the simplest shape is for `SetTags`/`Fail` to pass the target into `finishRun`. Tests: after `d.Show()` the canvas focus is the concept entry; after `Generating()` it is `cancelRunBtn`; after `SetTags`/`Fail` it is no longer a button that left `d.buttons.Objects`.

steps.title: Enter in the single-line inputs starts a run
steps.details: In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go extract the Generate button's body into `func (d *TagsDialog) startGenerate()` (guarding `d.generating` and `d.generateBtn.Disabled()`), use it for the button and set it as `OnSubmitted` of `d.concept`, `d.location` and `d.pathEntry` — Fyne fires `OnSubmitted` on Return for single-line entries, so a user can type a concept and press Enter without reaching for the mouse, while Return in the multi-line Title/Keywords keeps inserting a newline. Tests in internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog_test.go: `d.concept.OnSubmitted("x")` (or a Return key event on the entry) runs OnGenerate once and puts the dialog into the generating state; a second submission while generating does nothing.

steps.title: Document the dialog's keys
steps.details: Extend the "Tags dialog" section of `helpRight` in internal/gui/ui/help.go with the keys the dialog now owns: `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` move between fields and buttons, `Space`/`Enter` press the focused button, `Enter` in Concept/Location starts a run, `Esc` closes, and keep `B`/`N` for background/cancel of a running generation. Mirror the same list in the "Keyboard Shortcuts" section of CLAUDE.md (the `B` and `N` bullets currently say "Tags dialog only" without saying that they now work from the dialog itself).

questions.question: Should the dialog focus the Concept field when it opens? It makes typing immediate but means the canvas letter shortcuts no longer reach the app while the dialog is up (they are blocked by shortcutsBlocked anyway). Assume yes unless told otherwise. Affects step 3.
Should Tab move out of the multi-line Title/Keywords fields, giving up the ability to type a literal tab character there? Assume yes unless told otherwise. Affects step 1.
questions.answer: Yes - Tab traverses; a literal tab in Title/Keywords is given up.

questions.question: Should Enter in Concept/Location/claude-path start a generation? Assume yes unless told otherwise. Affects step 4.
questions.answer: Yes - Enter in the single-line entries starts a run.

questions.question: Keep the global fallback (ui/shortcuts.go OnCancel/OnBlue -> app.handleCancel/handleBlue) now that the dialog answers N/B itself, or delete the tags branch of handleBlue? Assume keep — it still fires when a mouse click has left nothing focused. Affects step 2.

Keep the current button order (Close, Copy title, Copy keywords, Save JPEG, Generate), which is also the Tab order, or should Generate come first? Assume keep — the existing test asserts that exact slice. Affects steps 2 and 3.

risks: glfw.GetKeyScancode returns -1 when GLFW is not initialised (unit tests, headless CI), so a scancode-only match would make N and B indistinguishable; the helper must also compare fyne.KeyName.

Bare letters cannot be intercepted inside a text entry: the driver delivers TypedKey and TypedRune separately, so swallowing KeyN in TypedKey would still insert 'n'. Only the buttons and the check may claim letters.
The button row is rebuilt by setGenerating; if focus stays on a button that was removed from the container, the focus manager keeps pointing at it and keys silently go nowhere.
canvas.Focus on a widget whose dialog is not shown logs an error - the focus helper must be a no-op until Show().
Escape from the date entry while the Fyne calendar popup is stacked on top must keep going through OnEscape -> app.handleCancel, which is the only place that can see the foreign overlay.

Existing tests compare d.buttons.Objects by identity and call test.Tap on the buttons; changing the field type to *dialogButton keeps both working only if the wrapper embeds widget.Button and calls ExtendBaseWidget.

todos.description: Copy stock tags from one photo to another
todos.context: Let a user take the stock tags of one photo (model.Tags - Title + Keywords, plus a Place on the todo/9 branch) and apply them to another photo; today there is no UI affordance and no core entry point for it, only per-photo generation. The pieces to build on are the Tags dialog session in internal/gui/app/tags_action.go, which owns the clipboard copies and the save path, the per-photo cache in internal/core/imaging/image_provider.go (PeekStockInfo/StoreStockInfo), and the writers ExifService.WriteStockTags (JPEG XMP packet with an EXIF fallback) and imaging.WriteSidecar (.xmp beside the RAW pair). Todo #9 is adding a Place to model.Tags and reshaping the sidecar and packet property tables, so whatever is copied has to carry the place too.

plan.summary: Add a way to take the stock tags of one photo (model.Tags: Title, Keywords and the Place that already landed on main) and apply them to another. The work splits into a core write entry point and an app-level "tag clipboard". In internal/core/imaging a new ApplyStockTags puts one model.Tags onto a photo through the two existing writers - WriteSidecar for the .xmp beside the RAW pair and ExifService.WriteStockTags for the JPEG's XMP packet - and reports what it actually wrote, while model.Tags gets a Clone so a keyword slice is never shared between the clipboard, the cache and a dialog. In internal/gui/app an in-memory tagsClipboard is filled by a new copy action (reading the per-photo cache, falling back to imageProvider.StockInfo on a worker goroutine) and drained by a paste action that confirms first - reusing showConfirm/dialogBlocked exactly like Delete and Copy - then writes on a worker goroutine through the existing saveTags helper, refreshes the per-photo cache (StoreStockInfo) and the overlay (setTagsIfCurrent), and reports the same rewritten/place-dropped notes Save JPEG already reports. The keys, the photo context menu, the help dialog and CLAUDE.md are wired last, and the Tags dialog finally gets a Paste button so the copied tags can be reviewed and edited before the existing close/Save JPEG paths write them.

steps.title: Core: clone tags and add the apply entry point
steps.details:
In internal/core/model/tags.go add `func (t Tags) Clone() Tags` returning the value with `slices.Clone(t.Keywords)` (Place is a value struct and needs nothing); this is what keeps a copied set from aliasing the cache entry that clonedStock in internal/core/imaging/image_loader.go guards today. Add the case to internal/core/model/tags_test.go: appending to the clone's keywords leaves the original alone, and Place survives the clone.

Add internal/core/imaging/stock_apply.go with a StockApply struct (embedding StockWrite plus Sidecar and JPEG bools) and `func (s *ExifService) ApplyStockTags(photo model.Photo, tags model.Tags, intoJPEG bool) (StockApply, error)`. It writes the sidecar with `imaging.WriteSidecar(model.SidecarPath(photo.RAWPath), tags)` when `photo.HasRAW()`, then, when `intoJPEG && photo.IsJPEG()`, calls `s.WriteStockTags(photo.ImagePath, tags)` and copies its StockWrite into the result. Both attempts run even if the first fails and the errors come back joined with errors.Join, so a half-written photo is still reported truthfully; the flags say which file was actually touched. Trap: WriteStockTags takes s.access.Lock itself, so ApplyStockTags must not hold that mutex (Go mutexes are not reentrant) - it only calls the two writers.

New test file internal/core/imaging/stock_apply_test.go, table-driven over (has RAW, intoJPEG): a RAW pair gets an .xmp holding title, keywords and the place levels; a JPEG with intoJPEG=true has the tags in its packet (reuse writePlainJPEG/writeJPEGWithTags and packetOf from exif_write_test.go/exif_service_test.go); a JPEG without a RAW pair and intoJPEG=false writes nothing and reports a zero StockApply; a failing JPEG write (path pointing at a non-JPEG) still leaves the sidecar in place and returns an error.

steps.title: App: the tag clipboard and the copy action
steps.details:
New file internal/gui/app/tags_clipboard.go holding a `tagsClipboard` struct (tags model.Tags, source string, filled bool) and a `tagsCopy tagsClipboard` field on Application in internal/gui/app/app.go. `func (a *Application) handleCopyTags()` guards with `a.shortcutsBlocked()`, takes `a.navigator.Current()`, and fills the clipboard from `a.imageProvider.PeekStockInfo(photo.ImagePath)`; on a cache miss it reads on a worker goroutine with `a.imageProvider.StockInfo(photo)` (logging a read error the way tags_view.go does) and finishes inside fyne.Do. Tags that are `nothingToWrite` (the helper already in tags_action.go) leave the clipboard untouched and show `a.mainWindow.ShowWarning(photo.Name + " has no tags to copy")`; otherwise the clipboard takes `info.Tags.Clone()` plus the source name and the user hears `ShowNotification("Tags of " + photo.Name + " copied")`. Nothing here waits for a pending generation - what is on disk or in the cache is what gets copied.

New test file internal/gui/app/tags_clipboard_test.go using newTestApplication/testPhoto from tags_runs_test.go: after StoreStockInfo and `a.navigator.SetPhotos([]model.Photo{photo})`, handleCopyTags fills a.tagsCopy with title, keywords and place; a photo with empty tags leaves it unfilled; the copied keyword slice is independent of the cached one; and handleCopyTags does nothing while a dialog is open (a.dialogs.open(...)).

steps.title: App: paste onto the current photo, confirmed and written
steps.details:
Add `dialogPasteTags` to the dialogKind block in internal/gui/app/dialogs.go. Add `func NewPasteTagsDialogContent(source, target string, isJPEG, hasRAW bool, tags model.Tags) (*fyne.Container, *widget.Check)` to a new internal/gui/ui/paste_tags_dialog.go, shaped like NewDeleteAllDialogContent in bulk_dialog.go: a bold "Apply the tags of <source> to <target>?" line, a wrapped summary line (title, keyword count, place), and a "Write into the JPEG" check that is only added for a JPEG, pre-checked when the photo has no RAW pair (otherwise nothing would be written at all). When `tags.Problems()` is not empty the content adds a warning label so the user knows the copied set does not meet the stock rules the Save JPEG button enforces.

In internal/gui/app/tags_clipboard.go add `func (a *Application) handlePasteTags()`: `a.dialogBlocked(dialogPasteTags)` guard (so a second press of the key confirms, like Delete), current photo, and a warning when the clipboard is empty. On confirm it runs through the existing `a.saveTags(a.tagsCopy.tags.Clone(), photo.Name, save, failed)`: the save func first `a.stopTags(photo)` - a generation still running for the target would otherwise overwrite what was just pasted, and stopTags waits, which is why it belongs on saveTags' goroutine - then `a.exifService.ApplyStockTags(photo, saved, intoJPEG)`, then the cache/overlay refresh, and returns `writeNote(res.StockWrite)` so the rewritten/place-dropped notes reach the user unchanged. The failed callback calls `a.imageProvider.Forget(photo.ImagePath)`, the same way tagsSession.saveSidecar does, so a failed write leaves no tags in the cache. Extract the cache+overlay pair out of tagsSession.storeStock in internal/gui/app/tags_action.go into `func (a *Application) storeStockInfo(path string, written model.Tags, taken time.Time)` and let both callers use it; the date comes from `a.imageProvider.PeekStockDate(photo.ImagePath)`.

Tests in internal/gui/app/tags_clipboard_test.go: pasting onto a photo with a RAW pair writes the .xmp (assert.FileExists on model.SidecarPath) and puts the tags in the cache; pasting with the JPEG box off leaves the JPEG bytes untouched; a paste with an empty clipboard writes nothing.

steps.title: Wire the keys, the context menu and the help
steps.details: Add `OnCopyTags` and `OnPasteTags` to ShortcutCallbacks in internal/gui/ui/shortcuts.go and map them to `glfw.GetKeyScancode(glfw.KeyX)` and `glfw.GetKeyScancode(glfw.KeyV)` - both letters are still free next to F/R/G/B/D/C/N/S/H/Y/L/Z/T/I. Add the same two to ContextMenuCallbacks in internal/gui/ui/contextmenu.go as "Copy Tags" and "Paste Tags" menu items next to "Generate Tags", and return the Paste item in ContextMenuItems so the app can set `Disabled` on it; internal/gui/app/navigation.go sets `a.contextMenuItems.PasteTags.Disabled = !a.tagsCopy.filled` in handleSecondaryTap before ShowContextMenu. Wire both callbacks to a.handleCopyTags/a.handlePasteTags in the SetupShortcuts and NewContextMenu calls in internal/gui/app/app.go. Add `{"X", "Copy stock tags"}` and `{"V", "Paste stock tags"}` to the Actions section of helpLeft in internal/gui/ui/help.go, and the same two lines to the Keyboard Shortcuts list in CLAUDE.md plus a sentence in the Stock tags feature paragraph describing what a paste writes (sidecar always, JPEG packet only when the confirm dialog's box is ticked).

steps.title: Paste into the Tags dialog for review before saving
steps.details: Give the dialog the reviewed path: add `OnPaste func()` to TagsDialogCallbacks and `CanPaste bool` to TagsDialogOptions in internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go, build a `pasteBtn` ("Paste tags") in buildButtons that is disabled when CanPaste is false, and include it in the idle branch of buttonSet after copyKeywordsBtn. Add `func (d *TagsDialog) PasteTags(pasted model.Tags)` that calls showTags(pasted) without finishRun (SetTags is the run's own path and renames Generate), so the fields, the location and the split are filled and refreshStatus re-gates Save JPEG. In internal/gui/app/tags_action.go pass `CanPaste: a.tagsCopy.filled` and an OnPaste that hands `a.tagsCopy.tags.Clone()` to the dialog; from there the existing paths do the writing - close() -> saveSidecar for the RAW pair, the Save JPEG button for the packet - so no new write path appears. Tests: internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog_test.go asserts PasteTags fills title, keywords and location and that the paste button is absent/disabled without CanPaste; internal/gui/app/tags_action_test.go asserts a session opened with a filled clipboard pastes into the dialog and that closing it writes the sidecar.

questions.question: Are X (copy stock tags) and V (paste stock tags) the right keys? They are free and layout-independent like the rest, but X reads as "cut" elsewhere. Assume X/V unless told otherwise. Affects step 4.

Should a paste ask for confirmation at all, or write straight away like a generation does? Assume a confirm dialog (Paste (V) / Cancel (N)), because a paste overwrites tags that are already on the target. Affects step 3.

Should the JPEG's XMP packet be written by a paste? Assume yes, but only behind the dialog's "Write into the JPEG" check, pre-ticked only for a photo with no RAW pair - the existing rule is that the JPEG is never written to without an explicit action. Affects step 3.
Should a paste carry the Place as well as Title and Keywords? Assume yes, whole model.Tags including the place, since copying between shots of one shoot is the point. Affects steps 1-3.
What should a paste do when a generation is still running for the target photo? Assume it cancels the run and waits for it (a.stopTags), so the run cannot overwrite the pasted tags. Affects step 3.
Should the clipboard survive an app restart (stored in preferences)? Assume no, in memory only. Affects step 2.
Should there be a bulk "paste onto all filtered photos", like Delete All / Copy All? Assume no, out of scope for this todo. Affects step 3.

Should the paste refuse to write into the JPEG when the copied tags fail model.Tags.Problems() (the gate the Save JPEG button uses)? Assume no - it warns in the confirm dialog and lets the user through. Affects step 3.

risks: ExifService.WriteStockTags takes s.access.Lock itself; ApplyStockTags must not hold that mutex around the call or it deadlocks.

Keyword slices are shared by reference: the clipboard, the cache and the dialog must all take a clone, otherwise editing tags in one place changes them in another (the reason clonedStock exists in image_loader.go).

Writing the JPEG can rewrite the whole file when the XMP packet has no room, which forces a Sony camera to re-index; the paste must surface rewrittenNote/placeDroppedNote through writeNote instead of a bare success.
A failed write must Forget the cache entry, or a later dialog reads tags from the cache that no file holds and never writes them again.
The tag clipboard is stored on Application and touched from both the UI goroutine and the read goroutine of the copy action; every store and every overlay refresh has to happen inside fyne.Do.
Both new keys go through shortcutsBlocked, so they do nothing in grid mode or with a dialog open - which is why step 5 adds the in-dialog Paste button.

Todo #10 reshapes the Tags dialog button row (types and the asserted button slice) and todo #13 reworks what the dialog saves on close; step 5 touches the same code and will conflict at merge if either lands first, though neither is a prerequisite.
golangci-lint's unused check would flag the new handlers before step 4 wires them; the tests added in steps 2 and 3 are what keeps them used (run.tests is true in .golangci.yml).

todos.description: Make sure tags edited by hand in the Tags dialog are written into the XMP
todos.context: Hand-edited Title and Keywords reach the RAW sidecar only when the dialog closes - tagsSession.close calls saveSidecar(s.dialog.Tags()) in internal/gui/app/tags_action.go, guarded by photo.HasRAW and skipped when the tags equal s.saved - while the run-finished paths write the sidecar from the run result instead (runFinished and the detached tagRunner.finishDetached in internal/gui/app/tags_runs.go). The JPEG's embedded XMP packet is written only through the explicit Save JPEG button (OnSaveJPEG -> tagsSession.saveJPEG -> ExifService.WriteStockTags), a button that exists only for a JPEG and is enabled only while model.Tags.Problems() is empty, so hand edits to a JPEG that are merely closed never enter the packet. Values come from TagsDialog.Tags(), which reads the live entry text, and every successful write also refreshes the per-photo cache through StoreStockInfo.

plan.summary: Hand edits in the Tags dialog currently reach disk only through two narrow paths: `tagsSession.saveSidecar` (RAW sidecar only, on close) and the explicit Save JPEG button (`ExifService.WriteStockTags`, enabled only while `model.Tags.Problems()` is empty). A JPEG whose fields were edited and then merely closed keeps nothing, and a JPEG without a RAW pair has no store at all. The plan adds an in-place-only stock tag write to `internal/core/imaging` - the same guarantee the Favorite toggle already gives: patch the embedded XMP packet where it has room, keep the file's size, layout, inode and modification time, and refuse rather than rewrite the whole file - then routes every implicit save (dialog close, run finished with the dialog on screen, backgrounded run) through one helper that puts the tags into the RAW sidecar and into the JPEG packet, updating the per-photo cache only when at least one file actually took them. The Save JPEG button keeps its role as the explicit write that may fall back to the EXIF and rewrite the file, and stays gated by `Problems()`.

steps.title: Add an in-place-only stock tag write to the imaging package
steps.details: In internal/core/imaging/exif_write.go extract the packet lookup that `WriteStockTags` already does (`os.ReadFile` + `xmpPacketSpan` + `packetWithTags`) into a shared helper, and add `func (s *ExifService) WriteStockTagsInPlace(jpegPath string, tags model.Tags) error` beside it, taking the same `s.access.Lock()`. It writes only through `patchPacket`, never through `replaceFileKeepingModTime`/`withStockTags`, and refuses with a new exported sentinel - e.g. `var ErrNoPacketRoom = errors.New("the XMP packet cannot hold the tags")`, wrapped with the file name via `%w` - in three cases: the file carries no packet (`start == end`), `packetWithTags` reports the packet closed or too small, and `exifShadows(original, tags)` is true (a field the user cleared would keep showing from the EXIF behind the packet, and clearing that needs a full rewrite). A packet that comes back byte-identical writes nothing and returns nil. Keep `WriteStockTags` behaviour unchanged. Tests in internal/core/imaging/exif_write_test.go, reusing `writeJPEGWithPacket`, `sonyPacket`, `readBytes`, `packetOf`, `sizeOf`: a roomy packet takes the tags in place (same length, same bytes outside the packet, EXIF untouched, mod time and `os.SameFile` kept, `GetStockInfo` reads them back); `sonyPacket(16)` returns `ErrNoPacketRoom` and leaves the file byte for byte; a JPEG with no packet (see `writeJPEGWithPacketOnly`'s counterpart in favorite_test.go for the layout helpers) returns the sentinel; clearing a title while the EXIF carries one returns the sentinel instead of rewriting the file.

steps.title: Route dialog saves through one helper that writes both the sidecar and the JPEG packet
steps.details: Add `stockTagWriter` to internal/gui/app/app.go - an interface with `WriteStockTags(string, model.Tags) (imaging.StockWrite, error)` and `WriteStockTagsInPlace(string, model.Tags) error`, held in a new `Application` field set to the `*imaging.ExifService` in `New()`, mirroring how `tagger tagGenerator` is held so a test can substitute a fake (`exifService` stays for `ToggleFavorite`). New file internal/gui/app/tags_files.go: `func (a *Application) writeTags(photo model.Photo, written model.Tags) (tagsWrite, error)` running on a worker goroutine, where `type tagsWrite struct { targets []string; note string }`. It calls `imaging.WriteSidecar(model.SidecarPath(photo.RAWPath))` when `photo.HasRAW()` and `a.stockWriter.WriteStockTagsInPlace(photo.ImagePath, written)` when `photo.IsJPEG()`, appending the base name of each file that took the tags to `targets`; an `errors.Is(err, imaging.ErrNoPacketRoom)` from the packet is not an error but a note ("the XMP packet of DSC001.JPG has no room - use Save JPEG to write them"), any other error is returned. In internal/gui/app/tags_action.go rename `saveSidecar` to `saveEdits`, drop its `!s.photo.HasRAW()` early return (keep the `written.Equal(s.saved)` and `nothingToWrite` guards and the optimistic `s.saved` bookkeeping), and let it call `writeTags`; update the two callers (`close`, `runFinished`). Change `Application.saveTags`'s save callback to return `(tagsWrite, error)` so the report can name several files: no targets and a note -> `ShowWarning(note)` plus the `failed` callback (revert `s.saved`, `imageProvider.Forget`) because no file holds the tags and the cache must not claim otherwise; targets with a note -> the existing "Tags saved to X - note" warning; targets alone -> the notification, joining the names with " and ". `saveJPEG` returns `tagsWrite{targets: []string{s.photo.Name}, note: writeNote(write)}`. `storeStock` is called only when at least one file took the tags. Tests in internal/gui/app/tags_action_test.go with a fake `stockTagWriter` recording calls: closing after an edit writes the packet of a JPEG-only photo and caches the tags; a JPEG+RAW photo gets both files; unchanged tags write nothing; an `ErrNoPacketRoom` on a photo with a RAW pair still saves the sidecar and caches; the same on a JPEG-only photo caches nothing and calls no error dialog.

steps.title: Let a backgrounded run write the JPEG packet as well
steps.details: In internal/gui/app/tags_runs.go replace the two write branches of `finishDetached` (the `!run.photo.HasRAW()` shortcut that only reports, and the inline `imaging.WriteSidecar` goroutine) with one goroutine calling `a.writeTags(run.photo, generated)` from step 2, keeping the existing ordering rules intact: `release(run)` right after the write returns and before `fyne.Do`, so a copy or delete waiting on the run finds every file already written; inside `fyne.Do` keep the `r.dropped(run)` check, report errors through `showError`, show `note` as a warning when the tags reached no file, and call `report` (cache + overlay + notification) only when at least one file took them. Tests in internal/gui/app/tags_runs_test.go: extend `newTestApplication` to accept or allow overriding the fake `stockTagWriter`, then assert that a backgrounded run on a JPEG without a RAW pair now writes the packet and only then stores the cache entry, that a run on a JPEG+RAW pair writes both, and that the existing "a sidecar that could not be written leaves the cache empty" case still holds.

steps.title: Update the documentation of what a save touches
steps.details: CLAUDE.md: in the Stock tags feature paragraph replace "a JPEG without a RAW pair is never written to on its own - that stays behind Save JPEG" with the new rule - closing the dialog and a backgrounded run put the tags into the RAW sidecar and, in place, into the JPEG's XMP packet where it has room; only the whole-file rewrite (the EXIF fallback) stays behind Save JPEG, which is still gated by the stock requirements. README.md: adjust the "Metadata written to files" paragraph the same way, spelling out that the packet write keeps the file's size, layout and directory entry like the favorite toggle does, and that a packet with no room is reported and left alone until Save JPEG is pressed.

questions.question: Step 2/3: should closing the dialog really write into the JPEG's XMP packet by itself, given CLAUDE.md's current rule that the JPEG stays behind the Save JPEG button? Assume yes, restricted to in-place patches that keep the file's size, layout, inode and modification time (the guarantee the Favorite toggle already makes), with the whole-file rewrite still behind the button, unless told otherwise.

Step 2: should the implicit packet write happen even when `model.Tags.Problems()` is non-empty (fewer than 50 keywords, empty title)? Assume yes - the sidecar is already written whatever state the fields are in, and the button's gate only guards the destructive rewrite.
Step 2: when the packet cannot take the tags and the photo has no RAW sidecar to fall back on, is a yellow warning naming Save JPEG the right report, or should it stay silent? Assume the warning.
Step 3: should a backgrounded run also write the packet, or only the dialog's own saves? Assume yes, so the same tags reach the same files whether the dialog was watching or not.

Should the app also push tags into a JPEG packet that lacks them when the dialog opens with tags that came from the sidecar alone and the user changes nothing? Assume no - only what the user or a run produced this session is written.

risks: Writing the JPEG on close changes a policy the code comments defend at length ("the file is the photo itself"); the in-place restriction is what keeps a Sony body from demanding a Recover Image DB, so the implicit path must never fall through to `withStockTags`/`replaceFileKeepingModTime`.

`exifShadows` means a cleared title on a JPEG whose EXIF still carries one cannot be honoured in place; refusing there is safe but leaves the old title visible until Save JPEG is used - the warning text must say so.

Cache poisoning: `StoreStockInfo` marks tags as "the file has them" and stops the next dialog from writing them again, so the store must stay behind a successful write on both the new skip path and the error path (the existing `Forget` compensation covers the sidecar today).

`finishDetached` ordering is load-bearing for copy and delete (`release` before `fyne.Do`, `dropped` check inside it); folding two writes into one goroutine must not move `release` earlier or later than the last file write.

App tests build fake JPEGs out of plain bytes, so any test that ends up on the real `ExifService` will see a parse error where it used to see nothing; the `stockTagWriter` fake keeps existing cases unaffected but `newTestApplication` needs the seam.
Todo #12 (copy stock tags between photos) will likely want the same `writeTags` helper; naming and signature should be kept general enough not to be rewritten there.
